image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a large adult common iguana resting on a rough, sandy rock surface near water. The iguana is facing right, displaying its profile. It has a prominent dorsal crest with reddish-orange spines on the neck transitioning to grey/black along the back. The skin texture is highly detailed with granular scales and larger plate-like scales on the head and limbs. A large dewlap hangs from the throat. The front left limb is clearly visible with distinct clawed digits. The background shows blurred blue water with small waves.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana displays adult coloration: greyish-brown/green tones with darker banding on the legs and body, rather than juvenile bright green.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent serrated crest runs from the neck down the spine. The spines are particularly large and colorful (orange/red) on the neck.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution detail shows fine granular texture on the body and larger, smoother polygonal scales on the face and snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front left limb is fully visible, showing long toes with sharp claws. The count of 5 digits is visually verifiable on this limb.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame to the left; only the base is visible. Its full length and compression cannot be verified.
